title: Example 18-2: Isolated Capital Letters Are Emphasized

illustrates.quote:
When isolated letters are capitalized and emphasized (e.g., italics, bold, colored type, underlined, etc.):
a. Follow print for emphasis.
b. Insert a transcriber’s note giving basic information about print capitalization.

blocks.text: Capitalize titles used before a proper name and titles used in direct address.

Transcriber's note: "The symbol [transcriber-defined red-letter mark] represents red letters." — back-translation of the given braille (louis.backTranslate) confirms the note's own wording matches the rule's own quoted Sample verbatim ('The symbol .=@#2 represents red letters.'); the mark itself (@#2, a second transcriber-defined symbol) cannot be minted by Emboss at all (F-188, only one hardcoded transcriber-defined symbol exists in the whole codebase) — not modeled.

print.notes: The list's own three titles each need the same undoable @#2 mark placed immediately before them (F-188); built here as plain text so the wording itself can still be checked, even though the mark cannot be.
print.printFeatures: Isolated capital letters (G, C, P, M) printed in red.

braille.notes: Re-extracted from source (lines 14360-14366, margin 9); matches both runs byte-for-byte — no correction needed here.

resolution: Both runs already agreed on braille.lines byte-for-byte; independent re-extraction from source confirms it exactly, so kept as-is. print.blocks rebuilt around buildModel18's own vocabulary: the intro sentence is an ordinary paragraph (representable); the TN sentence defining the @#2 symbol, and the symbol itself before each name, are F-188 (no second transcriber-defined symbol can be minted) — the note is recorded as 'other' since its wording is meaningless without the symbol it defines, while the three titles are still built as a plain list (wording testable, the missing @#2 prefix an expected, documented mismatch).
